storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Enterprise
storyOrder.summary: Set before the Federation, this series chronicles the early days of space exploration with Captain Jonathan Archer and the first Warp 5 starship, Enterprise NX-01.
storyOrder.trivia: The show's theme song, "Where My Heart Will Take Me," was a controversial departure from traditional orchestral themes.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Discovery
storyOrder.summary: Set a decade before TOS, this series follows Michael Burnham, Spock's adoptive sister, and the crew of the USS Discovery during the Federation-Klingon war.
storyOrder.trivia: The show's visual style, particularly the Klingon redesign, was a topic of much debate among fans.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds
storyOrder.summary: This series returns to an episodic format, chronicling the adventures of Captain Pike, Spock, and Number One aboard the USS Enterprise.
storyOrder.trivia: The show was created due to overwhelming fan demand for these characters after their appearance in Discovery.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: The Original Series
storyOrder.summary: The voyages of the starship USS Enterprise, on a five-year mission to explore strange new worlds, seek out new life and new civilizations, and to boldly go where no man has gone before.
storyOrder.trivia: Featured the first interracial kiss on American television between Captain Kirk and Lt. Uhura.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: The Animated Series
storyOrder.summary: The further animated adventures of the USS Enterprise crew, continuing where the original series left off.
storyOrder.trivia: It won a Daytime Emmy Award, a first for any Star Trek series.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: The Motion Picture
storyOrder.summary: A massive alien entity called V'Ger approaches Earth, and Admiral Kirk must reassume command of the Enterprise to stop it.
storyOrder.trivia: This film had a budget of around $44 million, making it one of the most expensive films of its time.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
storyOrder.summary: Kirk's arch-nemesis, Khan Noonien Singh, returns to seek revenge and seizes a powerful terraforming device.
storyOrder.trivia: The Genesis Device presentation was the first fully CGI sequence in a feature film.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
storyOrder.summary: After Spock's sacrifice, the Enterprise crew risks everything to find him and restore his living spirit.
storyOrder.trivia: This film marked Leonard Nimoy's directorial debut.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
storyOrder.summary: To save Earth from a destructive alien probe, the crew must travel back in time to 1986 to find humpback whales.
storyOrder.trivia: The most lighthearted and comedic of the original films, it was also the most financially successful.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: The Next Generation
storyOrder.summary: Set a century after the original series, this show follows the adventures of the USS Enterprise-D under the command of Captain Jean-Luc Picard.
storyOrder.trivia: Patrick Stewart was so convinced the show would fail that he didn't fully unpack his bags for the first six weeks.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
storyOrder.summary: Spock's half-brother hijacks the Enterprise to search for a mythical planet at the center of the galaxy, believed to be Eden or Heaven.
storyOrder.trivia: Directed by William Shatner, the film is often considered a low point for the movie franchise by fans and critics.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
storyOrder.summary: The Enterprise crew is framed for the assassination of the Klingon Chancellor, threatening a new era of peace between the Federation and the Klingon Empire.
storyOrder.trivia: The final film to feature the entire original cast.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: The Next Generation
storyOrder.summary: The adventures of the Enterprise-D continue, with many episodes delving deeper into the characters and the political landscape.
storyOrder.trivia: This season features the famous episode "Chain of Command," where Picard is tortured by the Cardassians.

storyOrder.title: Crossover Point!
storyOrder.content: Start watching Deep Space Nine. Alternate between new episodes of TNG and DS9.
storyOrder.summary: As The Next Generation enters its later years, a new series begins, set on a space station. The timelines run concurrently.
storyOrder.trivia: DS9 begins during TNG's 6th season.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: Commander Benjamin Sisko is assigned to a former Cardassian space station orbiting the planet Bajor, guarding a newly discovered stable wormhole.
storyOrder.trivia: Unlike other Trek series, it is set on a space station, not a starship, leading to more serialized storytelling.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: The Next Generation
storyOrder.summary: The final season of TNG wraps up long-running character arcs and concludes with the critically acclaimed finale, "All Good Things...".
storyOrder.trivia: The finale was watched by over 30 million viewers.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: The station becomes a key strategic location as the political and military threat from the Gamma Quadrant begins to grow.
storyOrder.trivia: The introduction of the Dominion as a major antagonist sets the stage for the rest of the series.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Generations
storyOrder.summary: Captain Picard and the TNG crew must stop a scientist from destroying a star system, leading to a fateful meeting with Captain Kirk.
storyOrder.trivia: Malcolm McDowell, who played the villain Soran, received death threats from fans for killing Captain Kirk.

storyOrder.title: Crossover Point!
storyOrder.content: DS9 continues. Now, start watching Voyager.
storyOrder.summary: As DS9 hits its stride, another series, Voyager, begins. Both shows run in parallel for several years.
storyOrder.trivia: The pilot of Voyager aired just two months before the DS9 Season 3 finale.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: The Dominion War looms as the USS Defiant is introduced, giving the crew a powerful warship to explore the Gamma Quadrant.
storyOrder.trivia: This season marked a turning point for the series, becoming darker and more focused on the impending war.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Voyager
storyOrder.summary: The USS Voyager is thrown 70,000 light-years across the galaxy into the Delta Quadrant and must begin a long journey home.
storyOrder.trivia: The first Star Trek series to feature a female captain, Kathryn Janeway, in the lead role.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: The Klingon Empire becomes a major antagonist, and Worf from TNG joins the station's crew.
storyOrder.trivia: The episode "Trials and Tribble-ations" digitally inserted the DS9 cast into the classic TOS episode "The Trouble with Tribbles".

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Voyager
storyOrder.summary: The crew continues to navigate the dangers of the Delta Quadrant, facing new species and internal conflicts.
storyOrder.trivia: This season explores the uneasy alliance between the Starfleet and Maquis members of the crew.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: First Contact
storyOrder.summary: The Borg travel back in time to prevent humanity's first contact with aliens. The Enterprise-E crew must follow them to stop their plan.
storyOrder.trivia: Widely considered the best of the TNG movies, it was a critical and commercial success.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: The Dominion War begins in earnest, pushing Sisko and his crew to their limits in a galactic-scale conflict.
storyOrder.trivia: This season features some of the largest and most complex space battle sequences seen in Star Trek up to that point.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Voyager
storyOrder.summary: Voyager encounters formidable new foes and finds new ways to survive in the hostile Delta Quadrant.
storyOrder.trivia: Features the popular two-part episode "Scorpion," which introduces the Borg's enemy, Species 8472.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: The war with the Dominion rages on, with major victories and devastating losses for the Federation and its allies.
storyOrder.trivia: The season-long arc is one of the most serialized and acclaimed storylines in Star Trek history.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Voyager
storyOrder.summary: The former Borg drone, Seven of Nine, joins the crew, bringing new dynamics and conflict to the ship.
storyOrder.trivia: Jeri Ryan's addition as Seven of Nine was a ratings boost and she became one of the show's most popular characters.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Insurrection
storyOrder.summary: Captain Picard and the crew defy a Starfleet admiral to protect a peaceful planet and its fountain of youth from being exploited.
storyOrder.trivia: The plot is often described by fans as feeling like an extended, two-part episode of the TV series.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
storyOrder.summary: The final season brings the epic Dominion War to a close and provides conclusions for the show's beloved characters.
storyOrder.trivia: The series finale, "What You Leave Behind," is a poignant and well-regarded conclusion to the saga.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Voyager
storyOrder.summary: In its final seasons, Voyager gets closer to home, facing final challenges and making a daring attempt to end their journey.
storyOrder.trivia: The finale, "Endgame," features an alternate future where Admiral Janeway gives her past self a major technological advantage.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Nemesis
storyOrder.summary: Captain Picard confronts a new Romulan leader who is a younger clone of himself, leading to a final, tragic battle for the TNG crew.
storyOrder.trivia: This was the final film for the TNG cast. Tom Hardy played the villain, Shinzon, before his rise to superstardom.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Lower Decks
storyOrder.summary: An animated comedy focusing on the low-ranking crew of one of Starfleet's least important ships, the USS Cerritos.
storyOrder.trivia: The show is packed with in-jokes and references to almost every previous Star Trek series and movie.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Prodigy
storyOrder.summary: An animated series following alien teenagers who discover a Starfleet ship, the USS Protostar, and are guided by a hologram of Captain Janeway.
storyOrder.trivia: This is the first Star Trek series to be co-produced with Nickelodeon Animation Studio.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Picard
storyOrder.summary: Decades after Nemesis, a retired Jean-Luc Picard is drawn back into a dangerous new adventure to help a mysterious young woman.
storyOrder.trivia: The third and final season served as a full reunion for the main cast of The Next Generation.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek: Discovery
storyOrder.summary: The Discovery crew travels to the 32nd century, a future where the Federation is a shadow of its former self.
storyOrder.trivia: This time jump effectively rebooted the show, allowing for entirely new stories unconstrained by established canon.

storyOrder.title: Note: Kelvin Timeline
storyOrder.content: The following films are reboots in an alternate reality. Watch them anytime.
storyOrder.summary: J.J. Abrams' movies created an alternate timeline after a Romulan ship from the future destroyed the USS Kelvin, allowing for new stories with the original characters.
storyOrder.trivia: Leonard Nimoy appears as Spock Prime, connecting the two timelines.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek
storyOrder.summary: A young James T. Kirk and Spock must overcome their differences to stop a vengeful Romulan from the future.
storyOrder.trivia: This film was the first Star Trek movie to win an Academy Award (for Best Makeup).

storyOrder.title: Star Trek Into Darkness
storyOrder.summary: The Enterprise crew pursues a one-man weapon of mass destruction, leading to a confrontation that reimagines a classic Star Trek villain.
storyOrder.trivia: The identity of the villain, played by Benedict Cumberbatch, was a closely guarded secret before the film's release.

storyOrder.title: Star Trek Beyond
storyOrder.summary: The Enterprise is destroyed by a ruthless new enemy, stranding Kirk and his crew on an uncharted planet.
storyOrder.trivia: The film was co-written by Simon Pegg, who also plays Scotty.
